title: Kuperberg-type qubit sieve for general N with proved 2^(4 sqrt n) poly(n) bounds

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, Algorithm DCP-SIEVE of proof.md (a Kuperberg-type qubit sieve with integer labels, a phase-estimation implementation of the Fourier-basis measurement, the parameter choice of proof.md Section 2 (explicit functions of N computed by the algorithm), and exhaustive shift testing for N <= 16) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 19/20 >= 2/3. With n = ceil(log2 N), its worst-case total work in the challenge cost model, on every execution branch (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gate synthesis, gates, measurements, source acquisitions at n+1 each, addressing and all failed attempts), satisfies T(N,s) <= C * 2^(4*sqrt(n)) * n^6 for an absolute constant C. Hence the uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n^6 and T = O(B_T); the growth index of this envelope is exactly 1/2 (log2 log2 B_T = (1/2) log2 n + O(log log n)). The constant 4 and the degree 6 are proved upper bounds, not tight. This holds jointly, for the same algorithm and parameter choice, with the classical-space, quantum-space and sample bounds below.

For the same Algorithm DCP-SIEVE of proof.md (a Kuperberg-type qubit sieve with integer labels, a phase-estimation implementation of the Fourier-basis measurement, the parameter choice of proof.md Section 2 (explicit functions of N computed by the algorithm), and exhaustive shift testing for N <= 16) and the same parameter choice, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak number of allocated classical bits on every execution branch (stored labels, sorting workspace, counters, gate descriptions and all other classical data) satisfies S_C(N,s) <= C * 2^(4*sqrt(n)) * n^2 for an absolute constant C, with n = ceil(log2 N). Hence the envelope is B_C(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n^2 and S_C = O(B_C); its growth index is exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time, quantum-space and sample bounds and the full-secret success probability at least 19/20.

For the same Algorithm DCP-SIEVE of proof.md (a Kuperberg-type qubit sieve with integer labels, a phase-estimation implementation of the Fourier-basis measurement, the parameter choice of proof.md Section 2 (explicit functions of N computed by the algorithm), and exhaustive shift testing for N <= 16) and the same parameter choice, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak number of allocated qubits on every execution branch (the retained sieve qubits plus the phase-estimation workspace) satisfies S_Q(N,s) <= C * 2^(4*sqrt(n)) * n^2 for an absolute constant C, with n = ceil(log2 N). Hence the envelope is B_Q(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n^2 and S_Q = O(B_Q); its growth index is exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time, classical-space and sample bounds and the full-secret success probability at least 19/20.

For the same Algorithm DCP-SIEVE of proof.md (a Kuperberg-type qubit sieve with integer labels, a phase-estimation implementation of the Fourier-basis measurement, the parameter choice of proof.md Section 2 (explicit functions of N computed by the algorithm), and exhaustive shift testing for N <= 16) and the same parameter choice, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every copy consumed by an aborted or failed attempt, satisfies Q(N,s) <= C * 2^(4*sqrt(n)) * n^2 for an absolute constant C, with n = ceil(log2 N) (each copy also pays n+1 work units inside the time bound). Hence the envelope is B_samples(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n^2 and Q = O(B_samples); its growth index is exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and the unconditional full-secret success probability at least 19/20.

For the same Algorithm DCP-SIEVE of proof.md (a Kuperberg-type qubit sieve with integer labels, a phase-estimation implementation of the Fourier-basis measurement, the parameter choice of proof.md Section 2 (explicit functions of N computed by the algorithm), and exhaustive shift testing for N <= 16) and the same parameter choice, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: every one of the Q acquired source copies is an independent ideal coset state rho_s for the same N and s. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 19/20 jointly with all four resource bounds above. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
